title: Watch: Hero ICE Officer Saves Drowning 6-Year-Old in Florida Pool
text:
A hero ICE officer made a snap decision to leap into a Florida pool when he spotted a 6-year-old struggling to stay afloat.
The act of heroism comes as the agency faces intense criticism and protests outside immigration facilities.
A Split-Second Rescue Gregory Simmonds was at a community pool in Pasco County on Florida’s Gulf Coast.
He noticed a young child floating unconscious in the water.
Closed-circuit footage showed Simmonds look over and, without hesitation, jump in fully clothed.
He quickly reached the child to render aid.
He carried the child back to the edge of the pool.
The child was resuscitated on dry land.
A 6-year-old boy was saved from drowning in a pool in Pasco County, Florida, after an ICE officer saw him floating unconscious and jumped in to rescue the child, according to the Department of Homeland Security. After taking the boy out of the pool, ICE officer Gregory Simmonds… pic.twitter.com/kMM7Va8Uma
— CBS News (@CBSNews) June 16, 2026
Life-Saving Care Simmonds is an officer with ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations office in Tampa.
He administered CPR to the child until they regained consciousness.
The child is now expected to make a full recovery, according to ICE.
“This officer swiftly sprung to action and delivered life-saving medical care to this 6-year-old who drowned,” said Acting Assistant DHS Secretary Lauren Bis.
She praised the agency’s officers as “the best of the best.”
She said sanctuary politicians should thank ICE rather than demonize it.
Praise from Local Police Pasco County Sheriff’s Office Cpl. J. Leathers credited Simmonds’ quick thinking.
He cited the officer’s “willingness to place himself into action during a critical incident.”
“His actions directly contributed to saving the life of the child,” Leathers said.
Gregory Simmonds
He said the response reflected “exceptional courage and selflessness.”
The statement was obtained by Fox News Digital.
The child’s survival was attributed directly to the officer’s decisive actions.
Not an Isolated Act Simmonds’ heroism is the latest example of DHS officers saving lives on the spur of the moment.
In March, an agent supporting the TSA at JFK Airport helped save a 1-year-old experiencing a medical emergency.
The agent “sprang into action and saved [their] life,” according to Sen. Markwayne Mullin.
In February, multiple off-duty ICE agents saved another child from drowning at a Minnesota hotel pool.
The agents performed CPR for several minutes until police and EMS arrived.
The cases highlight agents stepping up far from their enforcement duties.
Heroism Amid Backlash The rescues come as ICE agents face mounting protests.
Demonstrators have gathered outside facilities like New Jersey’s Delaney Hall.
Some have labeled the agents “fascists” and “mercenaries.”
Officials say the criticism ignores the daily risks agents take.
“Our ICE officers show up every day to protect the Homeland and their fellow Americans,” officials said of the backlash.
